meta.about: Godrej Agrovet Limited is a diversified, Research & Development focused agri-business company, dedicated to improving the productivity of Indian farmers by innovating products and services that sustainably increase crop and livestock yields. It holds leading market positions in the different businesses in which it operates - Animal Feed, Crop Protection, Oil Palm, Dairy and Poultry and Processed Foods. [1]
meta.keyPoints: Business Segments[1] [2] a) Animal Nutrition (46% in FY26 vs 48% in FY25): [3] [4] [5] The company is among India’s largest organised animal feed manufacturers, offering a diversified portfolio of cattle, layer, broiler, shrimp, fish and other animal feed products. It also has a presence in Bangladesh through its JV, ACI Godrej Agrovet Pvt Ltd. During FY26, the company introduced Dhanalaxmi G, a premium cattle feed targeted at high-yielding cattle, and Bypro Plus, an advanced high-protein formulation. The company’s sales volume in this segment increased from 14,75,144 tonnes in FY25 to 16,46,545 tonnes in FY26.
pros: Company has been maintaining a healthy dividend payout of 49.1%

company.profile: Diversified agri-business of the Godrej Industries group (incorporated 25-Nov-1991; listed Oct-2017 at ₹460). Six reported segments: Animal Nutrition (compound feed for cattle, poultry, fish and shrimp; India's largest organised cattle-feed maker), Vegetable Oil (India's largest crude palm oil producer from ~80,000 ha of farmer-owned plantations in AP, Telangana and other states), Crop Care (standalone branded agrochemicals plus 67.03%-owned listed Astec LifeSciences), Dairy (Creamline Dairy, 'Godrej Jersey', South India, 99.78% owned), Poultry & processed foods (Godrej Foods: Real Good Chicken, Yummiez; 100% owned since Aug-2024) and Others. 50% JV ACI Godrej Agrovet (Bangladesh feed). Holding company: Godrej Industries Ltd (65.05%).

FFB volume growth high single digit to early double digit for 4-5 years; area ~80,000 ha to ~1,50,000 ha (17,000 ha added in FY26); ~50% of plantations juvenile (0-4 years); Q1 margin dip from a state pricing-formula change; specialty-fats refinery from end-Aug/Sep-2026; downstream to add ~200 bp to overall EBITDA margin at scale; projects need 16-18% IRR.

60-70% of commodity inflation passed on; EBIT guidance ₹2,050-2,150 per tonne; cattle feed ~55-56% of volume, fish ~7%; poultry cut in chosen geographies; part of Q1 benefit from 'smart' buying 'may not be exactly structural'.
FY27 revenue growth 'at least more than 20%'; CDMO orders shifting to H2; CDMO ~50-52% of revenue; enterprise margins normalising as raw-material advantage fades.
Milk procurement prices high for 4 quarters and expected to stay for 2-3 more; ~70% passed on; war-led packaging inflation; 18-20 month route-to-market reset under a new CEO.
Live-bird trading to be cut 15-20% a year to near zero over ~5 years; B2C (Yummiez, RGC) 32% of the business, growing ~20%+; 3-4 years of investment phase; frozen chicken and momos launched.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Godrej Agrovet (consolidated, Rs crore). Built by reported segment: Animal Nutrition, Vegetable Oil (oil palm), Crop Care (standalone, i.e. the consolidated Crop Care segment less Astec), Astec LifeSciences (67.03%-owned, listed), Dairy (Creamline), Poultry & processed foods (Godrej Foods) and Others, plus a line that removes inter-segment sales. Segment EBITDA = segment result (PBIT) + segment D&A from the Ind AS 108 note; group EBITDA = sum of segments less central costs, on Screener's basis (other income below EBITDA). History is attributable to owners (Screener Net Profit replaced by Profit for EPS, see tools/authoring/GODREJAGRO.patch.js). Valued on sum of the parts, as the street does (Motilal Oswal Aug-2026, ICICI Securities): each business on Sep-28E EV/EBITDA, Astec at market value less a 20% holding-company discount, the ACI Godrej JV on P/E, less net debt.

segments.name: Animal Nutrition
segments._why: FY26 revenue +3% on volume +12% (16.5 lakh t; cattle feed +18%) and lower realisations; Q1FY27 revenue +12.6% on volume +7% (cattle feed +15%, fish +20%; poultry cut by choice) and realisations +5% as maize rose. Guidance (May/Aug-2026): double-digit, volume-led revenue growth. FY27 +11%, FY28 +9% (volume ~8%, price ~1%), FY29 +8%.
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA margin 5.2% (FY20), 7.6% (FY21), 6.5% (FY22), 4.6% (FY23), 5.9% (FY24), 7.5% (FY25), 8.3% (FY26, incl. ~Rs9.5 cr of pet-food manufacturing income in Q4 and favourable commodity positions). Reported segment result per tonne Rs2,108 in FY26; guidance Rs2,050-2,150 per tonne (Aug-2026). Supplier-financing cost now sits in this segment (Q1FY27 reported 6.4% EBIT margin vs 7.8% underlying). 8.0-8.1% keeps EBIT per tonne at ~Rs2,050-2,100, the guided range, not the FY26 Q4 spike.

segments.name: Vegetable Oil (oil palm)
segments._why: Revenue incl. ~Rs90 cr of trading. FY26 +39% (FFB +19%, OER +70 bp, CPO realisation +9%, PKO +47%); Q1FY27 +29% (CPO Rs1,34,783/t, +18%; FFB flat after the driest June in decades). Guidance: FFB volume high single to early double digit a year for 4-5 years (area 80,000 ha to ~1,50,000 ha; ~50% of trees still juvenile), specialty-fats refinery from H2FY27. FY27 +18% (price + ~9% volume); FY28 +6% (volume +10%, CPO price assumed to ease from war-time levels); FY29 +10%.
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA margin 17.4% (FY20), 15.4% (FY21), 21.3% (FY22), 21.5% (FY23), 17.1% (FY24), 18.8% (FY25), 21.4% (FY26). Q1FY27 segment result margin 16.7% vs 18.9% (state pricing-formula change). Margin is price-linked: farmers are paid by a formula tied to CPO prices, so the company keeps a share of each price move. 20.5% in FY27 (high CPO), 19.5% in FY28-29 (price eases; OER and scale offset; downstream fats add little before FY29).

segments.name: Crop Care (standalone)
segments._why: Consolidated Crop Care segment less Astec (= standalone crop care net of sales between Astec and GAVL). Standalone revenue Rs764 cr (FY25), Rs772 cr (FY26, +1%); Q1FY27 -17% (cotton herbicide volumes after a 40% June rain deficit). New products (Ashitaka maize herbicide, Takai insecticide, Ghassnash soybean herbicide) were ~18-20% of Q1 sales; management will give FY27 guidance only after September. FY27 +3% (H2 on a weak base), FY28 +12%, FY29 +10% as the portfolio diversifies.
segments._marginWhy: EBITDA margin on this basis 30.3% (FY20), 28.5% (FY21), 23.1% (FY22), 16.4% (FY23), 35.0% (FY24), 43.3% (FY25), 32.8% (FY26). Standalone EBIT margin 40.3% (FY25), 29.1% (FY26), 31.7% (Q1FY27 vs 42.2%). Management targets a 26-27% standalone EBIT margin for FY27 (~29-30% on our basis). We take 28% for FY27 (weak Q1, monsoon still erratic in Q2) and 30% for FY28-29: in-licensed products earn less than in-house Hitweed, so the 40%+ of FY25 does not come back.

segments.name: Astec LifeSciences (67.03%)
segments._why: Astec (Screener consolidated): revenue Rs628 cr (FY23), Rs458 cr (FY24), Rs381 cr (FY25), Rs448 cr (FY26); Q1FY27 Rs83 cr (-9%). Astec guided >20% growth for FY27 on CDMO orders shifting to H2 (Aug-2026); we take 15%, 15%, 12%.
segments._marginWhy: Operating profit margin 16.3% (FY20), 20.2% (FY21), 22.7% (FY22), 12.3% (FY23), -1.3% (FY24), -17.3% (FY25), -0.9% (FY26; company EBITDA +Rs1 cr); Q1FY27 break-even. 3% / 7% / 9%: a slow recovery as CDMO utilisation rises; still far below the FY21-22 peak.

segments.name: Dairy (Creamline)
segments._why: Revenue Rs1,501 cr (FY23), Rs1,573 cr (FY24), Rs1,585 cr (FY25), Rs1,589 cr (FY26); Q1FY27 +11.4% (volume +8%; value-added products 49% of sales vs 42%). Route-to-market reset over 18-20 months under a new CEO. FY27 +9%, FY28-29 +8%.
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA margin 2.6% (FY20), 3.7% (FY21), 0.4% (FY22), -0.8% (FY23), 4.2% (FY24), 5.0% (FY25), 3.6% (FY26, incl. land-sale gains); Q1FY27 company EBITDA margin 1.5% (milk procurement prices up, war-led packaging inflation; ~70% of cost passed on). 2.5% / 3.5% / 4.0%.

segments.name: Poultry & processed foods (Godrej Foods)
segments._why: Revenue Rs1,003 cr (FY23), Rs986 cr (FY24), Rs826 cr (FY25), Rs768 cr (FY26) as live-bird trading is cut 15-20% a year; branded B2C (Yummiez, Real Good Chicken) ~32% of the business, growing ~20% in value. Q1FY27 +0.7%. FY27 +4%, FY28 +8%, FY29 +10% as branded outgrows the live-bird decline.
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA margin -9.3% (FY20), 6.9% (FY21), 2.8% (FY22), 3.4% (FY23), 6.5% (FY24), 6.0% (FY25), 6.5% (FY26); Q1FY27 company EBITDA margin 2.6% (input costs, advertising behind new products). Management: 3-4 years of investment (EBITDA plus advertising). 5.0% / 6.0% / 6.5%.

segments.name: Others (seeds, cattle genetics, windmills, real estate)
segments._why: Other businesses Rs54.6 cr (FY23) to Rs157.4 cr (FY26); seeds and cattle genetics are under strategic review. +5% a year.

segments.name: Inter-segment eliminations
segments._why: Sales between segments (mainly oil and feed ingredients) removed on consolidation: Rs637 cr (FY23), Rs565 cr (FY24), Rs474 cr (FY25), Rs410 cr (FY26). Grows with the group: +8%.
segments._marginWhy: Inter-segment profit is not separately disclosed: modelled at zero.

assumptions._unallocLabel: Central costs and other income inside segment results (sum of segment EBITDA less Screener EBITDA)
assumptions._unallocWhy: Sum of segment EBITDA less Screener EBITDA: Rs173 cr (FY23), Rs188 cr (FY24), Rs187 cr (FY25), Rs323 cr (FY26). It holds (a) unallocated corporate expenditure net of corporate income (Rs83 cr FY23, Rs166 cr FY24, Rs168 cr FY25, Rs240 cr FY26: strategy reset, SAP, wage code) and (b) other income booked inside segment results that Screener shows below EBITDA (FY26: land-sale gains ~Rs34 cr, pet-food manufacturing income ~Rs9.5 cr). We assume Rs300-320 cr: corporate costs stay at the FY26 level and segment other income normalises.
assumptions._capexWhy: Capex Rs359 cr (FY23), Rs384 cr (FY24), Rs225 cr (FY25), Rs297 cr (FY26, cash). Guidance: "close to Rs400 crores" in FY27 (May-2026), then Rs300-350 cr a year from internal accruals, ~75-80% growth capex and ~50% oil palm (integrated palm complex, specialty-fats refinery, nurseries).
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 D&A Rs229 cr = 5.4% of average gross block (Rs4,268 cr, incl. Rs320 cr of brands/goodwill that are not amortised); Q1FY27 Rs57 cr. 5.5% gives ~Rs250 cr / ~Rs270 cr / ~Rs290 cr as the new oil-palm assets are capitalised.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: The group has net debt (Mar-26: borrowings Rs1,574 cr incl. Rs106 cr leases, cash Rs302 cr, investments Rs115 cr incl. the ACI JV at Rs91 cr), so the treasury yield earns nothing in the model; interest is entered separately.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Screener other income (normal) Rs70 cr (FY23), Rs93 cr (FY24), Rs97 cr (FY25), Rs106 cr (FY26); Q1FY27 Rs27 cr. It includes the share of the ACI Godrej JV (Rs32 cr FY23, Rs52 cr FY24, Rs54 cr FY25, Rs40 cr FY26 after Bangladesh raised the tax rate to 27.5%), interest and dividends (~Rs18 cr) and other income inside segment results (pet-food manufacturing, scrap, grants). Rs115 / 125 / 135 cr as the JV recovers (Q1FY27 PBT +12%) and pet-food income runs for a full year.
assumptions._interestWhy: Finance cost Rs99 cr (FY23), Rs108 cr (FY24), Rs133 cr (FY25), Rs138 cr (FY26); Q1FY27 Rs30 cr. Debt rose to fund the Rs718 cr Creamline buyout (Q1FY26) but part of the working capital moved to supplier financing (whose cost sits in Animal Nutrition costs). Rs125 cr in FY27, falling as free cash flow (~Rs100-125 cr surplus after capex guided for FY27) repays debt.
assumptions._taxWhy: Underlying tax ~26% (FY25 27%, FY26 27%; Q1FY27 29% incl. a deferred-tax remeasurement; statutory 25.17%; Astec losses get no credit). The tax line also carries minorities (engine workaround): 32.97% of Astec's loss is borne by its other shareholders, which RAISES profit attributable to GAVL. Astec loss assumed ~Rs55 cr / ~Rs31 cr / ~Rs10 cr (FY27-29E), minorities' share ~Rs18 cr / ~Rs10 cr / ~Rs3 cr. So the line = 26% less those amounts as a share of PBT. Model EPS = profit attributable to owners / 19.23 cr shares.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Dividend Rs10 (FY24), Rs11 (FY25), Rs11 (FY26) a share: 45-53% of EPS. Management: "consistently good dividend... range of 48-odd percent", decided each year. 45%.

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts at one rate (cost of equity = WACC). GAVL has modest net debt (~Rs1,160 cr vs ~Rs12,000 cr market value, ~9% of capital). Cost of equity ~12.5% (beta 1.0: commodity-linked feed and palm oil, monsoon-dependent crop care) weighted ~91%, post-tax cost of debt ~6% weighted ~9% = ~11.9%, which beta 0.9 produces.
dcf._tgWhy: Feed, edible oil, dairy and protein demand grow with nominal food consumption: 5.5% nominal.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades to 8% by year 12 (volume 4-5% plus price).
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: Group EBITDA margin was 6-9% in FY20-26 (8.4% in FY26); 9% long run as oil palm and branded foods grow in the mix.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex 2.8% of revenue long run (FY22-26 average ~3.4%), depreciation 2.2% of revenue (FY26 2.2%).
dcf._yearsWhy: 12-year explicit/fade period: oil-palm plantations take 4-8 years to mature.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: CPO stays near war-time prices and FFB grows double digit; Crop Care's new products restore a 30%+ EBIT margin quickly; Astec's CDMO orders lift it back to high-single-digit margins; milk costs ease so Creamline earns 5%+.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: CPO prices fall back to pre-war levels (or import duties are cut again) while the farmer price formula holds; another poor monsoon keeps cotton-herbicide volumes down; Astec stays loss-making; milk procurement costs stay high.

parts.note: Seeds, cattle genetics, windmills: small and under strategic review; low multiple.

parts.name: Central costs (net of other income inside segments)
parts.metricLabel: Sep-28E central costs × the blended operating multiple
parts.note: Valued at the EBITDA-weighted average of the operating multiples, so the businesses are valued after their share of head-office cost.

parts.name: Astec LifeSciences: 67.03% at market value less holding-company discount
parts.metricLabel: 67.03% × ₹1,620 cr market value (₹722.75 × 2.24 cr shares on 30-Sep-2026) × (1 − discount)
parts.note: Street method (Motilal Oswal: market value less 20%). Discount 20% base, 10% bull, 30% bear. Astec's EBITDA is therefore not valued again and its 32.97% minority is not deducted again.

parts.name: Add back: Astec net debt inside consolidated net debt
parts.metricLabel: Astec Mar-26 borrowings ₹449 cr − cash ₹12 cr
parts.note: Astec's market value is already after its own debt; the consolidated net debt below includes it, so we add it back to avoid deducting it twice.

parts.name: ACI Godrej Agrovet (Bangladesh JV, 50%) on P/E
parts.metricLabel: GAVL's FY26 share of JV profit ₹40.18 cr × P/E 12x (bull 14x, bear 10x)
parts.note: Equity-accounted, unlisted; profit ₹110 cr (FY25) and ₹80 cr (FY26, 100%) as Bangladesh raised its tax rate; pays dividends. Motilal Oswal uses 11x EV/EBITDA.

parts.name: Less: ACI JV at book (inside model net cash)
parts.metricLabel: Carrying amount at Mar-26 (AR FY26 note 55A)
parts.note: The model's net cash counts investments (incl. the JV at book) as cash; the JV is valued separately above.

parts.name: Net debt at Sep-27E (model: cash and investments less borrowings incl. leases)
parts.metricLabel: ½ Mar-27E + ½ Mar-28E
parts.note: Mar-26: cash ₹302 cr + investments ₹115 cr − borrowings ₹1,574 cr (incl. ₹106 cr leases) = −₹1,157 cr.

methods.name: Sum of the parts
methods.why: How the street values Godrej Agrovet (Motilal Oswal Aug-2026, ICICI Securities): six businesses with very different economics, a listed loss-making subsidiary and an unlisted JV.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: House rule: the stock's one-year-forward P/E median since Apr-2021 is 26.5x (no trough years), cut by the 14% median de-rating of 12 feed, dairy, edible-oil and crop-protection peers at 30-Sep-2026 = 22.7x; bull 26.5x (no de-rating), bear 18x (the stock's FY28-window level). Applied to Sep-28E EPS.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 12-year FCFF at ~11.9% WACC (beta 0.9), terminal growth 5.5%, EBITDA margin fading to 9%, plus model net debt.

cover.headline: Two strong businesses, four ordinary ones, and a price that already assumes the turnaround works
cover.lead: Godrej Agrovet is India's largest cattle-feed maker and largest crude palm oil producer, with crop protection, a loss-making listed chemicals arm (Astec), a South Indian dairy and a chicken brand attached. In FY26 oil palm and feed earned 71% of segment EBITDA; dairy and foods earned 9% on 22% of revenue. Q1FY27 showed the swings: feed EBIT +30%, oil palm +14%, but crop care −38% after a dry June, and attributable profit fell 17%. A new CEO (from Sep-2025) is pruning the portfolio. We value the company the way the street does, as a **sum of the parts on Sep-28E EV/EBITDA (blended 11.4x), with Astec at market value less 20%**. That gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with HOLD.** P/E on the stock's own de-rated history (₹785) is higher, the DCF (₹537) lower. arguments.h: Oil palm is the best business, and a price-taker
arguments.p: Vegetable Oil earned ₹428 cr of EBITDA in FY26 (21.4% margin, ~66% return on segment capital) as FFB volume rose 19% and CPO realisations 9%. Q1FY27 CPO was ₹1,34,783/t (+18%), inflated by the Middle East war. Farmers are paid by a CPO-linked formula and domestic prices follow import costs: on 24-Sep-2026 the government halved the duty on crude palm oil (10% to 5%). We model margins of 20.5% / 19.5% / 19.5%; every point is ~₹1.0 of FY28E EPS.

arguments.h: Feed is a volume winner with thin margins
arguments.p: Animal Nutrition sold 16.5 lakh t in FY26 (+12%; cattle feed +18%) and earned an 8.3% EBITDA margin, helped by Q4 commodity buying and pet-food manufacturing income. Management guides EBIT of ₹2,050-2,150 a tonne; we model 8.0-8.1%. Part of the working-capital gain is supplier financing: payables rose ₹766 cr in FY26.

arguments.h: Crop care is shrinking and Astec still loses money
arguments.p: Standalone crop care EBIT fell from ₹308 cr (FY25) to ₹224 cr (FY26) and 38% in Q1FY27, as the cotton herbicide franchise met bad weather and new in-licensed products earn less. Astec lost ₹81 cr in FY26 (₹135 cr in FY25); its structure is "under evaluation". We model crop care margins of 28-30% (not the 40%+ of FY25) and a slow Astec recovery.

Brokers use SOTP: Motilal Oswal ₹675 (10-11x FY28E EV/EBITDA, Aug-2026). Our multiples come from the stock's own forward EV/EBITDA median since 2021 (15.4x) less the peers' 26% de-rating. Our FY28E EPS of ₹31.8 is 12% below Motilal Oswal's ₹36.0. At ₹624 the stock trades at 19.6x our FY28E EPS.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): Crop Care's FY27 outlook, which management promised once the cotton-herbicide season was clear (end-September).
Domestic CPO prices after the 24-Sep-2026 duty cut on crude palm oil (10% to 5%): the biggest swing factor for oil-palm margins.
Astec: the group said in May-2026 it would decide the "most optimal structure" for Astec and its chemicals business within two to three quarters.
Specialty-fats refinery ramp-up in H2FY27 and the integrated palm complex: the start of the downstream (value-added) strategy.
Milk procurement costs (Creamline) and the route-to-market reset; Godrej Foods' branded growth vs live-bird run-down.

sections.title: Six businesses under one roof, with very different economics

blocks.p: Godrej Agrovet (GAVL) sells to farmers and buys from farmers. **Animal Nutrition** makes compound feed for dairy cattle (55-56% of volume), poultry, fish and shrimp. **Vegetable Oil** buys fresh fruit bunches (FFB) from ~80,000 ha of oil palm planted by farmers in factory zones allotted by state governments, and crushes them into crude palm oil (CPO) and palm kernel oil. **Crop Care** sells branded herbicides, insecticides and plant-growth regulators (Hitweed for cotton, Gracia for chilli, new Ashitaka, Takai, Ghassnash) and consolidates 67%-owned **Astec LifeSciences**, a listed maker of agrochemical active ingredients and contract manufacturer (CDMO). **Dairy** is Creamline (Godrej Jersey milk, curd, paneer, flavoured milk in the South). **Poultry & processed foods** is Godrej Foods (Real Good Chicken, Yummiez). It also owns 50% of ACI Godrej Agrovet, a Bangladeshi feed maker (revenue ₹1,501 cr, profit ₹80 cr in FY26).

sections.title: Five markets, one common thread: farm commodities and the monsoon set the margin

blocks.p: GAVL does not sit in one industry. It buys and sells farm commodities in five markets, and in each the margin depends on prices it does not set. **Feed** competes with home-mixed feed and many regional players; costs are maize and soymeal, and maize now also feeds ethanol distilleries. **Palm oil** is the one market where India is short: domestic crude palm oil output was 3.80 lakh t in 2024-25 against a national target of 11.2 lakh t, so prices follow imports, and imports follow world prices and Indian duties. **Crop protection** is seasonal and monsoon-timed. **Dairy** is a procurement game: when milk is scarce, processors pay more than they can pass on. **Chicken** is mostly sold live and unbranded; branded frozen chicken is new.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** GAVL has **two genuine advantages**: the oil-palm franchise (state-allotted factory zones, farmer relationships built over decades, the best extraction rates in India, and plantations that take 4-8 years to replicate) and scale and sourcing skill in cattle feed. Crop care has a strong brand but a narrow product base. Dairy, chicken and Astec have **no moat today**. None of the businesses sets its own prices: feed and dairy pass on 60-70% of costs, oil palm earns a formula-linked share of a world price, and Indian import duties can move that price overnight. Expect a 15-20% ROE company whose profits swing with commodity cycles, not a compounding consumer franchise.

sections.title: Revenue has tripled since FY15; the margin has stayed stuck at 7-9%

blocks.p: Godrej Agrovet's revenue rose from ₹3,312 cr in FY15 to ₹10,233 cr in FY26, 10% a year over the last five years. Profit has grown more slowly and less smoothly. EBITDA margin has never been above 9% in twelve years: it was 9.0% in FY21, fell to 5.6% in FY23 when maize and soymeal spiked and Astec turned down, and recovered to 8.4% in FY26 on oil palm. Profit attributable to shareholders was ₹314 cr in FY21, ₹302 cr in FY23 and ₹473 cr in FY26 (EPS ₹16.3 → ₹15.7 → ₹24.6). Q1FY27 broke the run: revenue +9%, EBITDA ₹240 cr vs ₹270 cr, attributable profit ₹134 cr vs ₹161 cr, as crop care fell after a dry June.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean audit, but working capital, buyouts and one-offs need adjusting

bullets: **Supplier financing flatters cash flow.** Operating cash flow was ₹1,281 cr in FY26 against ₹864 cr of EBITDA, because trade payables rose ₹766 cr as Animal Nutrition moved to vendor invoice discounting. The financing cost now sits in segment costs, not interest (Q1FY27: reported feed EBIT ₹84 cr vs ₹102 cr "underlying"). Treat part of the payables as debt: on our reading net debt plus supplier credit is well above the reported ₹1,157 cr (the split is not disclosed).

**Buyouts shrink equity and lift ROE.** ₹953 cr paid above book value for the Godrej Foods and Creamline minorities went straight to equity (AR FY26 note 55B). ROE rose to 21% in FY26 partly because the denominator fell. CRISIL notes the hit to net worth and the rise in adjusted gearing to 0.81x.

**One-offs both ways in FY26.** Land-sale gains of ~₹34 cr sat inside EBITDA (company EBITDA ₹969 cr reported, ₹936 cr underlying); a ₹30 cr labour-code charge was exceptional. FY25 had a ₹15 cr long-term-incentive reversal. Company "EBITDA" includes other income; Screener's (₹864 cr, our model basis) does not.

**Other income inside segments.** ~₹9.5 cr a quarter of pet-food manufacturing income for Godrej Pet Care (a group company) is booked in other income but included in the Animal Nutrition segment result. We neutralise it through central costs in the model.

**Minorities run the "wrong" way.** Astec's minorities absorb a third of its losses, so attributable profit exceeded total profit by ₹28 cr in FY26. Screener's headline "Net Profit" (₹445 cr) and EPS (₹24.58 on ₹473 cr) are on different bases; we use attributable throughout.

**Related parties are small but real.** Sales to Godrej Industries ₹66 cr and to Godrej Pet Care ₹19 cr; expenses charged by Godrej Industries ₹25 cr (₹17 cr in FY25); dividends of ₹137 cr paid to the parent and ₹70 cr received from the ACI JV (FY26).
**Audit.** BSR & Co. (KPMG network); no qualifications; contingent liabilities ₹165 cr, mostly old excise disputes. Brands and goodwill (~₹320 cr) are not amortised and were not impaired in FY26.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Nothing suggests aggressive revenue recognition, and the auditor is clean. But three things make reported numbers look better than the underlying business: supplier financing in working capital, ROE inflated by buyouts charged to equity, and FY26 one-off land gains inside EBITDA. Our forecasts use Screener's EBITDA (no other income), attributable profit, and assume supplier credit stays at the Mar-26 level.

sections.title: Moderate debt, and a working-capital gain that suppliers' banks are funding

blocks.p: Net debt was ₹1,157 cr at Mar-2026 (borrowings ₹1,574 cr incl. ₹106 cr of leases, less cash ₹302 cr and investments ₹115 cr, which include the ACI JV at ₹91 cr), about 1.3x EBITDA. CRISIL rates the commercial paper A1+ and puts adjusted gearing at 0.81x (0.57x a year earlier) after the Creamline buyout. The company reports average net working capital down from 45 days (FY24) to 25 days (FY26) and 21 days in Q1FY27. Much of that is trade payables, which rose from ₹628 cr to ₹1,651 cr in two years: Animal Nutrition now uses vendor invoice discounting, i.e. its suppliers are paid early by banks and GAVL pays the banks later. That is cheap funding, but it is debt-like and can be withdrawn.

segments.name: Animal Nutrition

segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA margin 5.2% (FY20), 7.6% (FY21), 6.5% (FY22), 4.6% (FY23), 5.9% (FY24), 7.5% (FY25), 8.3% (FY26, incl. ~Rs9.5 cr of pet-food manufacturing income in Q4 and favourable commodity positions). Reported segment result per tonne Rs2,108 in FY26; guidance Rs2,050-2,150 per tonne (Aug-2026). Supplier-financing cost now sits in this segment (Q1FY27 reported 6.4% EBIT margin vs 7.8% underlying). 8.0-8.1% keeps EBIT per tonne at ~Rs2,050-2,100, the guided range, not the FY26 Q4 spike.

segments.name: Vegetable Oil (oil palm)
segments._why: Revenue incl. ~Rs90 cr of trading. FY26 +39% (FFB +19%, OER +70 bp, CPO realisation +9%, PKO +47%); Q1FY27 +29% (CPO Rs1,34,783/t, +18%; FFB flat after the driest June in decades). Guidance: FFB volume high single to early double digit a year for 4-5 years (area 80,000 ha to ~1,50,000 ha; ~50% of trees still juvenile), specialty-fats refinery from H2FY27. FY27 +18% (price + ~9% volume); FY28 +6% (volume +10%, CPO price assumed to ease from war-time levels); FY29 +10%.
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA margin 17.4% (FY20), 15.4% (FY21), 21.3% (FY22), 21.5% (FY23), 17.1% (FY24), 18.8% (FY25), 21.4% (FY26). Q1FY27 segment result margin 16.7% vs 18.9% (state pricing-formula change). Margin is price-linked: farmers are paid by a formula tied to CPO prices, so the company keeps a share of each price move. 20.5% in FY27 (high CPO), 19.5% in FY28-29 (price eases; OER and scale offset; downstream fats add little before FY29).

segments.name: Crop Care (standalone)

Standalone revenue Rs764 cr (FY25), Rs772 cr (FY26, +1%); Q1FY27 -17% (cotton herbicide volumes after a 40% June rain deficit). assumptions._unallocLabel: Central costs and other income inside segment results (sum of segment EBITDA less Screener EBITDA)
assumptions._unallocWhy: Sum of segment EBITDA less Screener EBITDA: Rs173 cr (FY23), Rs188 cr (FY24), Rs187 cr (FY25), Rs323 cr (FY26). It holds (a) unallocated corporate expenditure net of corporate income (Rs83 cr FY23, Rs166 cr FY24, Rs168 cr FY25, Rs240 cr FY26: strategy reset, SAP, wage code) and (b) other income booked inside segment results that Screener shows below EBITDA (FY26: land-sale gains ~Rs34 cr, pet-food manufacturing income ~Rs9.5 cr). We assume Rs300-320 cr: corporate costs stay at the FY26 level and segment other income normalises.
assumptions._capexWhy: Capex Rs359 cr (FY23), Rs384 cr (FY24), Rs225 cr (FY25), Rs297 cr (FY26, cash). Guidance: "close to Rs400 crores" in FY27 (May-2026), then Rs300-350 cr a year from internal accruals, ~75-80% growth capex and ~50% oil palm (integrated palm complex, specialty-fats refinery, nurseries).
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 D&A Rs229 cr = 5.4% of average gross block (Rs4,268 cr, incl. Rs320 cr of brands/goodwill that are not amortised); Q1FY27 Rs57 cr. 5.5% gives ~Rs250 cr / ~Rs270 cr / ~Rs290 cr as the new oil-palm assets are capitalised.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: The group has net debt (Mar-26: borrowings Rs1,574 cr incl. Rs106 cr leases, cash Rs302 cr, investments Rs115 cr incl. the ACI JV at Rs91 cr), so the treasury yield earns nothing in the model; interest is entered separately.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Screener other income (normal) Rs70 cr (FY23), Rs93 cr (FY24), Rs97 cr (FY25), Rs106 cr (FY26); Q1FY27 Rs27 cr. It includes the share of the ACI Godrej JV (Rs32 cr FY23, Rs52 cr FY24, Rs54 cr FY25, Rs40 cr FY26 after Bangladesh raised the tax rate to 27.5%), interest and dividends (~Rs18 cr) and other income inside segment results (pet-food manufacturing, scrap, grants). Rs115 / 125 / 135 cr as the JV recovers (Q1FY27 PBT +12%) and pet-food income runs for a full year.
assumptions._interestWhy: Finance cost Rs99 cr (FY23), Rs108 cr (FY24), Rs133 cr (FY25), Rs138 cr (FY26); Q1FY27 Rs30 cr. Debt rose to fund the Rs718 cr Creamline buyout (Q1FY26) but part of the working capital moved to supplier financing (whose cost sits in Animal Nutrition costs). Rs125 cr in FY27, falling as free cash flow (~Rs100-125 cr surplus after capex guided for FY27) repays debt.
assumptions._taxWhy: Underlying tax ~26% (FY25 27%, FY26 27%; Q1FY27 29% incl. a deferred-tax remeasurement; statutory 25.17%; Astec losses get no credit). The tax line also carries minorities (engine workaround): 32.97% of Astec's loss is borne by its other shareholders, which RAISES profit attributable to GAVL. Astec loss assumed ~Rs55 cr / ~Rs31 cr / ~Rs10 cr (FY27-29E), minorities' share ~Rs18 cr / ~Rs10 cr / ~Rs3 cr. So the line = 26% less those amounts as a share of PBT. Model EPS = profit attributable to owners / 19.23 cr shares.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Dividend Rs10 (FY24), Rs11 (FY25), Rs11 (FY26) a share: 45-53% of EPS. Management: "consistently good dividend... range of 48-odd percent", decided each year. 45%.

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts at one rate (cost of equity = WACC). GAVL has modest net debt (~Rs1,160 cr vs ~Rs12,000 cr market value, ~9% of capital). Cost of equity ~12.5% (beta 1.0: commodity-linked feed and palm oil, monsoon-dependent crop care) weighted ~91%, post-tax cost of debt ~6% weighted ~9% = ~11.9%, which beta 0.9 produces.
dcf._tgWhy: Feed, edible oil, dairy and protein demand grow with nominal food consumption: 5.5% nominal.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades to 8% by year 12 (volume 4-5% plus price).
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: Group EBITDA margin was 6-9% in FY20-26 (8.4% in FY26); 9% long run as oil palm and branded foods grow in the mix.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex 2.8% of revenue long run (FY22-26 average ~3.4%), depreciation 2.2% of revenue (FY26 2.2%).
dcf._yearsWhy: 12-year explicit/fade period: oil-palm plantations take 4-8 years to mature.

methods.why: How the street values Godrej Agrovet (Motilal Oswal Aug-2026, ICICI Securities): six businesses with very different economics, a listed loss-making subsidiary and an unlisted JV.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: House rule: the stock's one-year-forward P/E median since Apr-2021 is 26.5x (no trough years), cut by the 14% median de-rating of 12 feed, dairy, edible-oil and crop-protection peers at 30-Sep-2026 = 22.7x; bull 26.5x (no de-rating), bear 18x (the stock's FY28-window level). Applied to Sep-28E EPS.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 12-year FCFF at ~11.9% WACC (beta 0.9), terminal growth 5.5%, EBITDA margin fading to 9%, plus model net debt.
